l4_steps.name: Identify crew training requirements from profiles
l4_steps.input: Crew qualification records, regulatory expiry dates, new-hire roster
l4_steps.output: Training requirements matrix per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: Training needs identified ≥90 days before regulatory expiry for 100% of crew
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen stores expiry dates per qualification type but does not auto-generate training demand; planners must run manual extracts, creating lead-time risk when expiry windows cluster post-peak season

l4_steps.name: Build annual training schedule against roster windows
l4_steps.input: Training requirements matrix, published crew roster, training facility calendar
l4_steps.output: Draft annual training schedule with assigned cohorts and dates
l4_steps.kpi: Training schedule published ≥60 days in advance for 95% of planned events
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors Learning schedule does not have a real-time read of Jeppesen roster data; integration relies on nightly batch sync, causing scheduling conflicts when roster changes are made intra-day

l4_steps.name: Validate training slot availability vs expiry window
l4_steps.input: Draft training schedule, regulatory expiry dates per crew member
l4_steps.output: Approved training schedule or rescheduled cohort
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew members scheduled for training after regulatory expiry date
l4_steps.pain_point: Facility and simulator capacity at crew training centres frequently bottlenecks slot availability, particularly for SEP training requiring full-scale cabin mock-ups — often forces costly overtime or third-party centre bookings

l4_steps.name: Deliver SEP safety & emergency procedures training
l4_steps.input: Approved training schedule, current SEP syllabus per aircraft type, regulatory syllabus (FAR Part 121.433)
l4_steps.output: Completed SEP classroom and practical session records
l4_steps.kpi: SEP training completion rate ≥100% before regulatory expiry (FAR Part 121.433 mandatory); classroom session NPS ≥4.2/5.0
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 121.433 mandates annual SEP recurrent training; full-scale cabin mock-up availability at training centres is constrained — scheduling slippage >30 days past planned date has occurred during peak hiring periods

l4_steps.name: Conduct aircraft type-specific cabin familiarization
l4_steps.input: Aircraft configuration specs (B737-700/800/MAX 8), SEP completed status
l4_steps.output: Aircraft type familiarization sign-off per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of cabin crew type-qualified before first line assignment on that aircraft variant
l4_steps.pain_point: Fleet mix of B737-700 (-143 seats) and B737-800/MAX 8 (-175 seats) requires separate door and evacuation drills; adding MAX 8 MCAS awareness content required unplanned syllabus revision after 2019 grounding

l4_steps.name: Administer written safety knowledge assessment
l4_steps.input: Completed SEP and type familiarization sessions
l4_steps.output: Assessment score record per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: First-attempt pass rate (score ≥80%) ≥95% of cohort; average score ≥87%
l4_steps.pain_point: Assessment question bank in SAP SuccessFactors Learning is not versioned against specific regulatory revision cycles; outdated questions have appeared after FAA circular updates, requiring manual audit of question pools before each cohort

l4_steps.name: Evaluate safety assessment pass/fail and route remediation
l4_steps.output: Pass certification or remedial training assignment
l4_steps.kpi: Remedial loop resolved within 14 calendar days; zero crew deployed without confirmed pass
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew who fail on first attempt require additional classroom time that displaces scheduled cohorts; no automated re-booking logic in SAP SuccessFactors Learning forces manual calendar intervention

l4_steps.name: Deliver in-flight service standards curriculum
l4_steps.input: Service standards manual (current version), brand and product updates from inflight services team
l4_steps.output: Completed service standards classroom session record
l4_steps.kpi: Service standards curriculum delivered to 100% of active cabin crew within annual training cycle; session completion rate ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Inflight product changes (e.g. menu rotations, new beverage service procedures) are communicated via separate email distribution; SAP SuccessFactors Learning course content lags by 4–6 weeks, leaving a gap where crew operate on outdated standards

l4_steps.name: Train galley management and catering loading procedures
l4_steps.input: Catering loading specifications, galley configuration diagrams per aircraft type
l4_steps.kpi: Galley loading error rate on line flights ≤0.5% of sectors (measured via customer complaint and inflight report data)
l4_steps.pain_point: B737-700 and B737-800 have different galley configurations; training material must be aircraft-type-specific but SAP SuccessFactors Learning course library does not enforce type-level prerequisites, allowing crew to complete wrong-type galley module

l4_steps.name: Conduct mock in-flight service drill and evaluate
l4_steps.input: Completed service standards and galley modules, cabin mock-up facility booking
l4_steps.output: Service drill evaluation scorecard per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: Drill pass rate ≥90% first attempt; average service quality score ≥3.8/5.0 on evaluation rubric
l4_steps.pain_point: Mock cabin facility time is shared with SEP drills; scheduling conflicts cause service drills to be shortened or deferred, resulting in crew entering IOE with incomplete practical service training

l4_steps.name: Assign IOE line check flights with qualified evaluator
l4_steps.input: Drill pass scorecard, evaluator availability roster, open line flight schedule
l4_steps.output: IOE pairing assignment for new or recurrent check crew
l4_steps.kpi: IOE line check flights assigned within 10 days of practical training completion for 90% of crew
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualified cabin crew evaluators (check cabin crew) are drawn from operational roster — their availability conflicts with line flying duties; Jeppesen does not distinguish check crew duty type from line duty for optimisation purposes, causing evaluator shortfalls

l4_steps.name: Conduct IOE line check observation and scoring
l4_steps.input: IOE pairing assignment, IOE evaluation form, service standards scorecard criteria
l4_steps.output: Completed IOE observation report with scored competency ratings
l4_steps.kpi: IOE report submitted within 24 hours of check flight; evaluation criteria coverage ≥100% of mandatory competency items
l4_steps.pain_point: IOE evaluation forms are completed on paper and manually entered into IBS iCrew post-flight; transcription errors and late submissions (>48 hours) have created compliance gaps identified during FAA ATOS audit cycles

l4_steps.name: Evaluate IOE line check pass/fail threshold
l4_steps.input: Completed IOE observation report, minimum competency thresholds
l4_steps.output: Line check pass certification or additional IOE assignment
l4_steps.kpi: IOE first-attempt pass rate ≥88%; crew requiring >2 IOE attempts flagged for remediation programme review
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated escalation logic when crew fail second IOE attempt; Crew Training Manager must manually initiate extended remediation, which delays qualification by 3–6 weeks and increases cost per trained crew member

l4_steps.name: Issue FAA-compliant cabin crew qualification record
l4_steps.input: IOE pass certification, safety assessment pass, all module completions
l4_steps.output: Crew qualification certificate with next-due recurrency dates
l4_steps.kpi: Qualification record issued within 48 hours of final IOE pass; zero records issued with incomplete module pre-requisites
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 121 requires the operator to maintain individual crew training records that are producible on FAA request within 24 hours; IBS iCrew record completeness depends on all upstream systems having posted — batch sync gaps with SAP SuccessFactors create producibility risk

l4_steps.name: Synchronise training records across LMS and crew system
l4_steps.input: Qualification certificate, SAP SuccessFactors Learning completion records
l4_steps.output: Reconciled crew training record in IBS iCrew and SAP SuccessFactors
l4_steps.kpi: Record reconciliation completed within 24 hours of qualification issuance; discrepancy rate between systems ≤0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Nightly batch integration between SAP SuccessFactors Learning and IBS iCrew uses flat-file exchange without transaction-level error logging; silent failures result in qualification data appearing complete in LMS but absent in crew scheduling system, causing crew to be erroneously assigned flights

l4_steps.name: Validate FAR Part 121.433 recurrent compliance status
l4_steps.input: Reconciled crew training records, FAR Part 121.433 recurrency intervals by training type
l4_steps.output: Compliance status report — pass or non-compliant flag per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of active flying crew compliant with all FAR Part 121.433 recurrency requirements at all times; compliance dashboard accuracy ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 121.433 recurrency window calculations require tracking multiple qualification types (SEP, type, service) with different intervals; manual tracking in spreadsheets has been used as a backup when IBS iCrew reports are slow, introducing version-control risk

l4_steps.name: Apply scheduling restriction to non-compliant crew
l4_steps.input: Non-compliant crew flags from IBS iCrew compliance report
l4_steps.output: Scheduling hold applied in Jeppesen; crew notified via automated alert
l4_steps.kpi: Scheduling restriction applied within 2 hours of non-compliance flag; zero non-compliant crew assigned to revenue flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen scheduling hold must be manually applied by a crew compliance analyst — there is no automated API trigger from IBS iCrew non-compliance flags; overnight non-compliance identified after Jeppesen pairing optimiser has already run can result in non-compliant pairings requiring costly last-minute rebidding
